role.altitude: The remote sensing scientist keeps designing strategies and data models, judging image quality, deciding on operational changes and teaching technicians; searching catalogues, rebuilding processing chains, loading data by hand, checking every acquisition by eye and grading exercises shrink.
skills_to_grow: Writing reusable processing scripts and QC checks
role.ambitious_version: A scientist whose processing, loading and quality checks rerun by script, leaving time for method and judgement.

tasks.short: Review requirements and available data, design strategies for collection, analysis or display of geographic data, implement the processing workflow, and design the map display.

steps.what: Scientist reviews project requirements and searches available satellite and aerial data
Scientist designs the strategy for collection and analysis of geographic data: sensors, resolution, revisit and methods
Scientist designs the display of results: map layouts and dashboard views

tasks.design: The scientist searches the data space catalogue by area, date and cloud cover instead of several portals. Designing the strategy stays with the scientist. Processing is set up from rerunnable scripts over datacubes kept from earlier projects and adapted, instead of building each chain anew. Map layouts and dashboard views start from the team's style templates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data were searched portal by portal and processing chains rebuilt per project.
tasks.enabler_now: Datacube processing with rerunnable scripts and shared catalogues.
tasks.still_hard: Projects needing commercial or airborne data with custom specs.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the sensor and season that will show what the client needs.

evidence.claim: An EU data space offers rerunnable Python or R scripts over Sentinel datacubes.

assumptions: Boundary: designing and implementing strategies; processing imagery into products (task 18261) and analysing data (task 18256) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3: a script library from earlier projects kept by the team.
unknowns: Share of projects on open satellite data.

incremental.description: Scientist keeps the script library and templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: projects with custom airborne data; high: open satellite data with reused scripts.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design the data model, create the database tables, load project data, write metadata, and test and open access to develop or build databases for remote sensing or geospatial project information.

steps.what: Scientist designs the data model: layers, attributes and metadata fields
Scientist builds the database tables and spatial indexes
Scientist loads the project's imagery footprints and survey layers into the database
Scientist writes metadata records for the datasets
Scientist tests the database and gives users access

tasks.design: Designing the data model stays with the scientist. Tables and spatial indexes are created by a script from the data model, instead of by hand in the database tool. A load script imports imagery footprints and survey layers, checks projection, extent and required attributes, and lists what failed. Writing metadata belongs to the data documentation task and is priced there. Testing and access stay with the scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tables were created and files loaded one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Scripted database builds and validated loads.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a data model that will still fit the next project.

reach.learn: Whether loaded data are complete and consistent.

evidence.claim: Records apps with instrument import and specification checks replace paper and spreadsheet processes in labs.

assumptions: Boundary: building project databases; maintaining data and documentation (task 18260) and integrating other sources (task 18258) are sibling tasks.
s4 is part of maintaining geospatial data documentation, which sibling task 18260 covers; its saving is counted there.
Designing and testing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of legacy data with problems.

incremental.description: Scientist maintains the build and load scripts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much legacy data; high: clean new project data.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run quality checks on each acquisition, inspect sample images, compare with specifications and determine if procedural or equipment changes are necessary, and report findings to operations.

steps.what: Scientist checks quality metrics of each data collection: cloud cover, positioning accuracy and radiometry
Scientist determines whether procedural or equipment changes are necessary
Scientist reports findings and recommended changes to the operations team

tasks.design: A quality-check script runs on every acquisition and writes cloud cover, positioning residuals and radiometric statistics to a dashboard with the specification limits, instead of the scientist computing them in a spreadsheet. Visual inspection and the decision on changes stay with the scientist. The note to operations starts from the dashboard figures.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quality figures were computed by hand per acquisition.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a stripe pattern that points to a failing sensor.

ambition.what: Check every acquisition instead of a sample.

reach.learn: Whether problems are fixed before the next campaign.

evidence.claim: Scripted pipelines and report templates prepare charts and image data deterministically.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring collection quality; directing hardware operation (task 18263) and installation testing (task 18272) are sibling tasks.
Inspecting and deciding keep their full time.

incremental.description: Scientist maintains the quality-check script and limits.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few acquisitions with custom sensors; high: many routine acquisitions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare training material and exercises, train technicians in the use of remote sensing technology, score exercise results against reference data, and give feedback.

steps.what: Scientist prepares training material and exercises with sample data
Scientist trains technicians in the use of remote sensing technology
Scientist scores technicians' exercise results against reference data
Scientist gives technicians feedback on their work

tasks.design: Training uses notebooks and sample datasets kept from earlier courses, which the scientist adapts rather than building each exercise anew. A script compares each technician's classification or correction output with reference data and reports accuracy, so the scientist reviews scores instead of computing them. Teaching and feedback stay personal. Scores are for learning only, not for rating staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercises were rebuilt and scored by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable notebooks and scripted scoring against reference data.
tasks.still_hard: Technicians with very different starting levels.
tasks.human_edge: Showing why a classification went wrong.
tasks.altitude: Less preparation and scoring; teaching stays.

evidence.claim: Audit trails and records naming staff need works council consent if used to check performance.

assumptions: Boundary: training technicians; directing operation of systems (task 18263) is a sibling task.
Teaching and feedback keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of training sessions per year.
research_questions: Do technicians reach target accuracy sooner?

incremental.description: Scientist keeps reference data and notebooks current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new topics each time; high: repeat courses with reused exercises.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
